reason: I'll start with filtering to follow what leaves the blood before useful substances are recovered. The picture shows small substances can pass through narrow gaps.
expectation: I expect water, glucose, salts and some waste to pass into the filter space, while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters clearly start the route to the bladder, but I want to explore filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful substances through along with waste, so the recovery tube is the next step to follow.
reaction: It is interesting that filtering does not just remove waste.
reason: The tube's picture shows useful substances returning to blood, which directly continues the filtering goal.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, leaving waste in the tube.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the bladder route, but I want to finish following recovery first.

effect: Recovery returns useful substances and much water to the blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to collect.
reaction: The contrast between filtering and taking substances back makes sense.
reason: The ureters lead from the kidneys toward the bladder, so I'll start building that route.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidneys, leaving the bladder to be fitted next.

alternatives.reason: The bladder is also needed, but the ureters connect it to the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are attached and lead downward from the kidneys, ready for the bladder.
reaction: The route is straightforward so far.
reason: The bladder is the only offered combination and completes the drainage route.
expectation: I expect the bladder to connect to the ureters so urine can collect there.

effect: The kidneys now have a continuous route through the ureters to the bladder; the remaining fluid still needs to be collected.
reaction: The drop tracing the route makes the connection clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect the recovered fluid to the completed drainage route.
expectation: I expect the remaining waste-containing fluid to travel through the ureters and collect as urine in the bladder.

effect: The remaining fluid reached the bladder through the ureters, completing both the recovery and drainage routes.
reaction: Seeing urine and blood follow separate routes made the ending clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtering with recovery was most worthwhile: it showed that useful substances pass through the filter and then return to the blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was straightforward and the only offered combination, so it felt more like assembly than a decision.

surprise.text: The filter lets useful substances through along with waste, rather than selecting only waste.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the final collection was an obvious required combination rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would continue: the filter-and-recovery contrast made me curious about how other body systems work.
